newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end lower on strong yen.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end lower on strong yen.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures closed lower on Wednesday, damaged by the yen's strength against the dollar, traders said.
Prices ranged from 70 to 240 yen lower, with the benchmark May 1998 contract closing 220 yen down at 14,160 yen per tonne.
Light selling from local investors emerged particularly in distant months, traders said.
"The stronger yen discouraged local investors throughout the day," a brokerage trader said.
Rolling forward of positions ahead of the expiry in spot July contract, which expires on June 13, is likely to pressure the market this week, traders said.
The spot July corn contract on the CBOT Project A overnight trading system stood at $2.71-3/4 per bushel at 0645 GMT, unchanged from Tuesday's close.
Spot July CBOT soybean futures were trading at $8.14-1/2 a bushel at 0645 GMT, up from $8.13 at Tuesday's close.
